I need to build a knowledge base from recent papers about large language model fine-tuning and alignment. Please access our academic paper repository and read the full content of papers that are relevant to the topics of LLM fine-tuning, alignment, and model architecture improvements. For each relevant paper, read through its sections carefully to understand the methodology and key results. Skip any papers that are about unrelated topics like robotics or physical systems.

Create a Notion page titled LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base. The page should contain blocks for each relevant paper, where each block covers the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings from the paper.

Also create a Word document called LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx in my workspace. The document should start with a heading called LLM Fine-Tuning and Alignment Survey, followed by an introduction paragraph. Then include a dedicated section for each relevant paper that presents the paper title, the author names, a description of the method, and the key results extracted from reading the paper sections.

Finally, create a Google Sheet called LLM Paper Registry with columns for ArXiv_ID, Title, Authors, Published_Date, Key_Contribution, and Method_Category, with one row per relevant paper.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent itself runs the compact discovery queries, then uses one parallel full-text reader wave of three per-paper explorers and one parallel writer wave of three deliverable owners.

Before Wave 1, the main agent covers the task-relevant local arXiv candidate space in read-only mode through complementary fine-tuning, alignment, and architecture queries at the supported per-call bound; unions and deduplicates all returned IDs (the search exposes no cursor); applies the task's relevance rule (reject robotics or physical-system distractors); and freezes exactly three retained paper IDs — never importing outside facts or importing rejected IDs downstream.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per retained paper ID:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Reader for retained paper 1. Use the local repository read_paper tool with paper_id = that literal assigned ID, read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results, and return EXACTLY the structured report {paper_id, title, full authors, published date, key method, source-backed findings, method category, section coverage}. Read-only: do not create Notion, Word, Google Sheet, or intermediate files.
   2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): Reader for retained paper 2 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 2): Reader for retained paper 3 — same literal recipe, only paper_id substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies one handoff per retained ID, deduplicates titles, verifies every rejected paper against the exclusion rule, and freezes one normalized packet with per-paper controls.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the single Notion page exclusively. Search for LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base, create at most one page, add one substantive block per frozen paper with title, method, and findings, and read it back. Return page ID/title, paper coverage, block count, and validation. Do not write the Word document or Google Sheet.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own LLM_Paper_Synthesis.docx exclusively. Create it exactly once with the required heading, introduction, and one author/method/results section for every frozen paper. Read it back and return path, headings, retained-paper coverage, and validation. Do not modify Notion or Google Sheets.
3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Google Sheet LLM Paper Registry exclusively. Create it once with the exact six columns and one row per frozen paper, preserving full authors and source dates and using controlled Method_Category values. Read it back and return spreadsheet/sheet IDs, headers, row count, and validation. Do not write Notion or Word state.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile the same stable-ID set, authors, methods, and findings across all deliverables, verify every rejected paper appears nowhere, and complete only after file and external-state checks. Do not dispatch any further agent and do not add a verification wave.

You are a read-only academic literature researcher (explore agent) tasked with producing a structured report about ONE arXiv paper stored in the local paper repository.

CONTEXT: We are building a knowledge base about large language model (LLM) fine-tuning and alignment. Your assigned paper is "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model", arXiv ID 2305.20050, which is a core alignment/fine-tuning paper. This paper has been pre-validated as relevant; do not re-judge relevance.

YOUR TASK:
1. Use the tool mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper with paper_id = "2305.20050" to read the FULL content of the paper in markdown format.
2. Read through ALL sections of the paper (not just the abstract) to understand the methodology and key results. If the paper content is long, read the entire returned content carefully.
3. Return EXACTLY a structured report with the following fields:
   - paper_id: "2305.20050"
   - title: the paper's exact title
   - full authors: ALL author names as they appear in the paper (the list_papers summary may truncate authors; extract the complete author list from the full content if available; otherwise report what is available)
   - published date: the paper's published/submitted date as shown in the repository metadata or content
   - key method: a concise description of the core method introduced (e.g., how DPO works, the loss/objective, what makes it novel vs RLHF)
   - source-backed findings: the main results/findings, each grounded in specific sections of the paper (e.g., benchmark improvements, stability claims, specific numbers if stated)
   - method category: one controlled category label for the paper, chosen from: "Fine-Tuning", "Alignment", or "Architecture"
   - section coverage: list of the paper sections you actually read (e.g., section titles or numbers)

CONSTRAINTS:
- Read-only: do NOT create any Notion pages, Word documents, Google Sheets, or intermediate files. Do not write anything to disk.
- Do not use the online arXiv API tools (mcp__arxiv-latex__*); use ONLY the local repository tool mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper.
- Do not invent facts. Every finding must be traceable to the paper content you read. If the full author list is not available in the content, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

DELIVERABLE: Return the structured report as your final message, formatted as a labeled list or JSON with exactly the fields listed above.

You are an external-workflow operator (coder) owning ONE deliverable: a Notion page. Work exclusively with the Notion MCP tools (mcp__notion__*). Do NOT create or modify Word documents or Google Sheets, and do not write any files to disk.

GOAL: Create a Notion page titled "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base" containing one content block per relevant paper (3 papers). The paper set below is pre-validated and frozen — use ONLY this data, do not fetch or invent additional information.

FROZEN PAPER PACKET (source-backed from the academic repository; note: the repository exposes title/authors/date/abstract metadata for these papers, and full body sections are not stored — use the abstract-grounded descriptions below as the authoritative content):

PAPER 1:
- arxiv_id: 2305.20050
- title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
- authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma
- published_date: 2023-05-30
- key_method: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) — a stable, performant, and computationally lightweight alternative to RLHF that aligns language models to human preferences by directly optimizing the language model policy without explicit reward modeling.
- findings: Presents DPO as a stable, performant, computationally lightweight alternative to RLHF that directly optimizes the language model policy; positions implicit reward modeling / direct policy optimization as the mechanism for preference alignment (grounded in the paper abstract).

PAPER 2:
- arxiv_id: 2307.09288
- title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
- authors: Hugo Touvron, Louis Martin
- published_date: 2023-07-18
- key_method: Development and release of a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models ranging from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters; the fine-tuned models (Llama 2-Chat) are optimized for dialogue use cases through supervised fine-tuning and preference-alignment training.
- findings: Llama 2 is a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs spanning 7B to 70B parameters; Llama 2-Chat fine-tuned models are optimized for dialogue use cases (grounded in the paper abstract).

PAPER 3:
- arxiv_id: 2310.06825
- title: Mistral 7B
- authors: Albert Jiang, Alexandre Sablayrolles
- published_date: 2023-10-10
- key_method: A 7-billion-parameter language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency through architectural improvements (e.g., attention/efficiency design choices).
- findings: Mistral 7B outperforms the best open models of all sizes on all evaluated benchmarks (grounded in the paper abstract).

EXCLUSION RULE: A paper titled "Robot Learning with Affordances" (arxiv 2309.16349, robotics) was REJECTED from this knowledge base. It must NOT appear anywhere on the page.

STEPS:
1. Search Notion (mcp__notion__API-post-search, query "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base") for an existing page. If an existing page with exactly this title is found, reuse it. Otherwise create exactly ONE new page (mcp__notion__API-post-page) with parent type "page_id" only if you can locate a suitable parent page via search (e.g., a top-level page returned by a broad search); if no parent page exists, create it with parent type "workspace". The page title must be exactly "LLM Fine-Tuning Knowledge Base".
2. Add one substantive block per paper (3 blocks total). Each block must cover: the paper title, the key method introduced, and the main findings. Use structured blocks (e.g., heading_3 with the paper title, followed by bulleted_list_item or paragraph blocks with Method and Findings) appended via mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children on the page id.
3. Read the page back (mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page and/or mcp__notion__API-get-block-children) to validate content.

DELIVERABLE (return in your final message):
- page_id and page title
- paper coverage (which of the 3 papers appear, with their titles)
- block count on the page
- validation result (read-back confirmation that each paper's title, method, and findings are present, and that the rejected robotics paper 2309.16349 / "Robot Learning with Affordances" appears nowhere)
